title: Decision-making, barriers and facilitators regarding alternative care pathways for low-acuity patients in German emergency medical services: the GUIDE-EMS study
summary:
Emergency medical services also care for people who are not critically ill or injured and who may not need treatment in a hospital emergency department. In these situations, other appropriate options for further care may be possible, such as treatment by an outpatient doctor or another form of care outside hospital. However, deciding whether such an option is appropriate can be difficult for emergency medical staff.
This study investigates which difficulties paramedics in Germany experience when considering appropriate care outside a hospital emergency department for people whose condition is not time-critical. It also examines which factors may make such decisions easier and how confident paramedics feel when making these decisions.
Paramedics currently working in Germany will be asked to complete a one-time online questionnaire. The questionnaire covers their professional experience, perceived difficulties and helpful factors, and their experience with different options for further patient care. Some questions refer to emergency calls attended during the preceding seven days. No patients are examined as part of the study, and the study does not change the treatment or care provided to patients.
conditions: Care of non-time-critical patients in German emergency medical services and use of alternative care pathways outside the emergency department.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Qualification as a Notfallsanitäter:in in Germany.
• Current involvement in direct prehospital patient care in the German emergency medical service.
• Current clinical work at least partly on EMS response units that are not routinely staffed by a physician, with involvement in decisions about the patient's further care pathway.
• Current professional activity in Germany.
• Electronic informed consent to study participation, scientific analysis and publication, and the planned sharing of a de-identified study dataset in a scientific repository as described in the participant information.
Exclusion criteria:
• No current qualification as a Notfallsanitäter:in.
• No current direct prehospital patient-care activity, for example exclusively administrative, dispatch, management, teaching or research work.
• Current patient-care activity exclusively in settings where a physician is routinely part of the responding clinical unit and no independent non-physician EMS disposition decisions are made.
• Participation in the formal GUIDE-EMS cognitive pretest.
• No electronic informed consent.
